Prime Minister Donald Tusk said authorities arrested the suspect, who was alleged to have been recruited by the Russian secret service, on Aug. 7. Tusk said the suspect was recruited to kill the individual because they were “inconvenient to the Putin regime.” Recommended Stories US celebrates breakthrough as Syrian paramilitary group dissolves, signaling ‘bright future’ for once-fractured state ‘Butcher of Bosnia’ Ratko Mladic dies at 84 while serving life sentence in The Hague Thousands missing from dozens of countries after Nepal flooding In collaboration with the United States, Poland successfully stymied the attack targeting a U.S. citizen “of Ukrainian origin,” whose identity has not been revealed and who was said to have a U.S. and Ukrainian passport. Advertisement “At the last minute, thanks to the action of the Internal Security Agency and the police, we managed to prevent this execution, this attack,” Tusk said on Thursday. Russia has repeatedly denied allegations that it targets enemies abroad, dismissing such claims as Western countries fostering an anti-Russia perception. Tusk, however, said President Vladimir Putin would not shy from crossing borders to target people he sees as enemies of Moscow. “We must assume that the Putin regime will try to eliminate people who are inconvenient for various reasons, in various places around the world,” Tusk said. Advertisement In June, Moscow was accused of assassinating a Russian artist who was critical of Putin. Robert Kuzovkov, known by the pseudonym Semyon Skrepetsky, was shot at close range, and Tusk at the time said the killing reflected a political assassination. Poland, which has served as a military centerpiece for Ukraine as the war with Russia wages on, was recently struck by a Russian missile intended for Kyiv that impacted a field. RUSSIAN MISSLE STRUCK POLAND DURING LARGE-SCALE ATTACK ON UKRAINE: POLISH PRIME MINISTER Advertisement At the end of July, Russia launched an estimated total of 83 missiles of various types at targets across Ukraine, concentrating on Kyiv, Krivoy Rog, and Lviv, according to reports. One of those missiles, a Kh-101, was alleged by Polish authorities to have flown deep into Polish territory, over 50 miles past the Ukrainian border and striking the field. Russian attacks intended for Ukraine have spilled into Polish airspace throughout the war. The missile in late July was the first time a missile had directly impacted Polish territory. Polish leaders had a mixed response, as Tusk said the missile was intentionally allowed to make it that far into the country. However, Polish Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz characterized the incident as “an extremely tough night for our air defense, observation and threat detection systems.” The Washington Examiner reached out to the State Department for comment. https://www.mfa.gov.lv/en/global-gateway.text: Global Gateway Published: 26.08.2026. Global Gateway is the European Union’s (EU) strategy established with the aim of promoting sustainable and reliable connectivity in partner countries in the areas of digital development, climate and energy, transport, health, education and research. To promote smart, clean and secure connectivity, the EU is implementing the strategy through Team Europe approach to strengthen the role of EU Member States and their financial and development institutions in implementing the strategy, while engaging the private sector, civil society and other implementing partners. As a result, a joint EU offer is being developed in partner countries, which is essential both for providing targeted expertise and solutions for the development of partner countries and for the EU’s economic and security interests. A key role is assigned specifically to the systemic involvement of the private sector, with the aim of implementing sustainable projects – through investment and innovative solutions – that address the needs of partner countries and ensure the development of local communities. Since 2021, public and private sector investments mobilised under the Global Gateway have exceeded the initial target of EUR 300 billion for the period from 2021 to 2027. A new target of EUR 400 billion has now been set. Forms of private sector engagement The private sector can participate in the Global Gateway in the following ways: Investment project proposal from an EU company or a consortium of EU companies: A conceptual investment project proposal developed by the company must be submitted to the Latvia’s Team National contact point at TeamLatviaGG@mfa.gov.lv by completing the designated questionnaire. Participation in calls for proposals: The EU periodically issues thematic calls for investment proposals, which are organised after the EU and the relevant partner country have agreed on the investment needs in a specific sector and the potential involvement of the EU private sector. Calls for expression of interest are also organised. Participation in events: Companies are invited to participate in business forums and matchmaking events to identify potential cooperation opportunities and facilitate the formation of joint consortia involving companies from multiple EU Member States. Participation in calls for proposals Information on Global Gateway calls for proposals and tenders is available on the websites of each European Commission (EC) Directorate-General involved in implementing the Global Gateway, as well as on the joint tenders portal. Each of the EC’s Directorates-General has currently developed its own investment mechanisms and platforms. Through these, investment projects can be submitted by EU companies or consortia formed by multiple companies . Regions where investment project proposals can be submitted: Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America and Asia. Responsible Directorate-General – DG INTPA . Enlargement and Eastern Neighbourhood. Responsible Directorate-General – DG ENEST . Middle East, North Africa and the Gulf. Responsible Directorate-General – DG MENA . For countries under DG INTPA , coordination takes place through the Investment Hub. The conditions stipulate that the value of the investment project must be at least EUR 10 million, of which at least 10% must be covered by the company itself or the established consortium. Thematically, the project must fall within the areas of climate and energy, digitisation, transport, health, or education and research. DG ENEST ’s Investment Hub currently oversees country-specific calls for proposals, setting the minimum investment threshold and the required level of company participation for each case. The minimum investment threshhold of Ukraine’s reconstruction projects must be EUR 50 million, of which 30% must be provided by the investor. The key sectors are energy, critical minerals, manufacturing, construction materials, information technology and digital transformation, transport and logistics. For the Armenia call for project proposals, the minimum threshold is EUR 30 million, of which 20% must be own contributions. The key sectors are energy and climate, digitalisation, transport and logistics, health, education, manufacturing and agriculture. DG MENA manages separate regional and national investment platforms. Applications are currently open for a call for proposals aimed at gathering information on business interests in the region and proposed solutions in the fields of digitalisation, climate and energy, transport, health, education, research and other areas. The platforms in Egypt and Jordan are also active. Team Latvia regularly informs major business and industry associations, as well as government partners, about current calls for proposals and events. If your company is interested in being added to the mailing list that receives these emails, please write to TeamLatviaGG@mfa.gov.lv . Expressing interest is also important in cases where the investment amount is below the specified threshold, as it allows for discussions to begin, both at the national level and with the European Commission, regarding a potential project proposal and for exploring opportunities. Process for submitting investment project proposals If a company has an idea for an investment project outside the scope of a call for proposals, it may take the initiative and submit an investment project proposal, envisaging the project’s implementation in one of the partner countries. After an investment project proposal is evaluated at the national level (Team Latvia) against the established criteria, it is forwarded for evaluation to the relevant EC Directorate-General’s coordination and facilitation platform, Investment Hub, in the region, which provides guidance on potential support instruments. The Investment Hub facilitates coordination between companies and investment project support tools. The instruments provided by the European Investment Bank (EIB), the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and other European financial institutions most commonly offer loans and guarantees, as well as technical assistance for project development and political support. The decision to finance each project is made in collaboration with the European financial institution offering the appropriate support instrument or an EU mechanism, such as the European Fund for Sustainable Development Plus (EFSD+). Support for investment projects The support offered by the EC for investment projects, if approved, can be either financial or non-financial in nature. Financial support Loans, equity investments and guarantees provided by public or private financial institutions Technical assistance Depending on the specific project, support may be provided directly to an EU company (or consortium) or to its partners in the target country or region Non-financial support Political support and economic diplomacy Dialogue with local authorities (regulatory issues, investment-friendly conditions, market access) Technical assistance (feasibility studies, environmental, social and governance (ESG) assessments, project structuring) Prior coordination to promote EU participation in international competitive tenders Identification of European partners to form competitive consortia Additional information About Global Gateway : Global Gateway - European Commission Global Gateway flagship projects : Global Gateway projects - International Partnerships - European Commission Global Gateway: Council endorses flagship project list for 2026 - Consilium European Commission Directorate-General DG INTPA ( Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America, Asia) and the DG INTPA Regional Investment Hub ; Global Gateway Business Opportunities - International Partnerships . D4D Hub – On 13 December 2023, Latvia joined the Digital for Development ( D4D ) Hub. It is a key instrument for the EU and its Member States to achieve the Global Gateway strategy’s objectives in the field of digitalisation. This initiative allows Latvia to participate more actively in EU’s digital cooperation projects around the world. https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/15/anot.text: An oil tanker caught fire in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday after entering what Iran's navy described as a prohibited zone with its tracking systems disabled, Iranian state-run media reported, the second such incident in the area in 24 hours.Iran's navy said monitoring teams patrolling the eastern sector of the Strait of Hormuz detected the tanker ablaze in the restricted area, according to a statement cited by the Mehr news agency.The name, flag and crew condition of the vessel were not immediately known, nor was the cause of the fire.On Wednesday, Iranian domestic media reported a fire on another tanker near the Strait of Hormuz after it also switched off its tracking equipment.The incidents follow the sinking of two commercial vessels in the same waters in recent days. The container ship GFS Pride sank on Wednesday after catching fire. All 21 crew members were rescued.The IRGC said the vessel struck a sea mine, while maritime sources cited an unidentified projectile.The cargo ship Cape Dao, which had previously been struck by a projectile, also sank. One crew member was killed in the initial attack.Videos circulating on social media appeared to show cargo including mobile phones and luxury goods floating in the water near the Strait of Hormuz, with people in small boats collecting items.Multiple international media outlets published the footage, as well as separate footage of containers and debris in waters reportedly near the strait. Euronews could not independently verify its veracity.US Central Command (CENTCOM), which oversees US military operations in the region, had not commented on Thursday's incident as of publication.Tehran's expanded ban in place?Iran's IRGC declared the waters leading to the Strait of Hormuz a prohibited zone in September, following remarks by Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council.IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohbi said the zone covered part of the Gulf of Oman and part of the Arabian Sea along the approach to the strait.Ali Azmayi, commander of the IRGC naval force, said Tehran exercises "smart control" over the strait and that all vessels seeking to transit the route must obtain permission, in response to US statements that the waterway remains open and under Washington's control.Tehran has said vessels violating the rules in the area face penalties. Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz closed in late February at the start of the war with the US, which Washington followed up with its own naval blockade of the key waterway.
